sections.h2: Which Sherburne County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Two offices share the work, and both sit in the same building in Elk River. The Assessor sets each parcel's estimated market value and classification, and the Auditor/Treasurer bills and collects the tax. Both are at 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, Elk River, MN 55330-4668.

  • Assessor: 763-765-4900, for value, class and appeals
  • Auditor/Treasurer property tax division: 763-765-4350, for statements, payments and penalties

The county describes the Auditor/Treasurer role as calculating tax rates, preparing statements and "truth in taxation" notices, and keeping records of unpaid parcels. If a parcel stays unpaid, the same department takes judgment and runs forfeiture proceedings under state law. A seller usually needs both offices: the Assessor for any value dispute, the Auditor/Treasurer for a payoff figure before closing.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Sherburne County itself?
sections.html:
Sherburne County is a Minneapolis-St. Paul metro county in central Minnesota, with Elk River as its seat and largest city. It covers 451 square miles, of which 433 are land, and the terrain is low rolling hills dotted with lakes and ponds. Soil here carries a lot of sand and gravel, so farming plays a smaller part than in much of the state. The Mississippi River runs along the southern border, and the Rum River crosses the upper east side.

The county seat started out at Humboldt, the village now called Big Lake, and a county vote moved it to Elk River in 1867. Cities today are Baldwin, Becker, Big Lake, Clear Lake, Elk River, Zimmerman, and parts of Princeton and St. Cloud. Census QuickFacts gives this picture for buyers and sellers:

  • 104,194 residents as of July 2025, up 7.2% from the April 2020 base
  • 38,457 housing units, with 83.2% occupied by their owners
  • Median owner-occupied home value of $361,400 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median household income of $105,466, and a mean commute of 30.7 minutes
  • 319 building permits issued in 2025, on about 225 residents per square mile

The Rum and Mississippi river corridors, the lakes and the Sherburne National Wildlife Refuge are all inside the county line, so a parcel's setting can matter as much as the house on it.

sections.h2: When are Sherburne County property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is due in two halves: May 15 and October 15. Agricultural parcels pay the second half by November 15 instead. The county says a mailed payment counts only if the postmark is on or before the due date, and it warns that many post offices now postmark mail two or three days after pickup.

Real estate tax of $50 or less must be paid in full by May 15. Penalties start the day after a due date and climb in steps, as the county's schedule for a first-half payment shows:

Penalty on an unpaid first half, Sherburne County 2026 schedule (county Penalties page)

May 162%4%

A second-half balance left unpaid after October 15 starts at 2% for a homestead and 4% for other property. Farm homesteads that miss November 15 pay 6%, and non-homestead farmland pays 8%. If you are paying late, call the property tax division for the exact figure to include.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Sherburne County tax bill?
sections.html:
There are five routes, and the county's payment page lists each one. Mail goes to the Auditor/Treasurer at the Elk River address, with checks made out to the Sherburne County Auditor / Treasurer. In person, you can pay by check or cash at the property tax division in the Government Center, and an after-hours drop box sits by the main entrance (door A).

  • Online or by phone through Forte: 2.40% of the tax with a $2.00 minimum for credit cards, $1.55 per eCheck, and $4.00 for a debit card. The phone line is 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307, and you need the parcel ID from your statement.
  • Direct payment: the county withdraws May 15, October 15 (or November 15 for agricultural parcels) from your bank account. Paperwork must reach the Auditor/Treasurer by April 15 for the first half or September 15 for the second.
  • Escrow: if a lender collects tax in your mortgage payment, the lender pays the county. Ask your mortgage company if you are unsure.

A weekend or bank holiday due date shifts a direct withdrawal to the next business day. Cancelling direct payment also takes written notice by the same April 15 or September 15 cutoffs.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Sherburne County value or classification?
sections.html:
Start with a call to the Assessor, because the county's appeal steps begin with reviewing the evidence together. Gather a recent appraisal or sales of similar homes first. Then take your case to the local board named on your valuation notice. For 2026 those boards met in April, from Big Lake and Princeton city hearings on April 3 at the Government Center to Livonia Township on April 27, so this year's local round has passed.

  • Local Board of Appeal and Equalization: held at the city or township hall in April, and the notice tells you the date.
  • County Board of Appeal and Equalization: the 2026 session was Tuesday, June 16, with appointments only, booked through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351.
  • Minnesota Tax Court: a petition may be filed directly once you have your notice, no later than April 30 of the year the tax is payable. The court's phone is 651-296-2806.

Next year's schedule will be printed on the notice mailed in spring. The Assessor also posts a re-assessment tool at gis.co.sherburne.mn.us/AssessmentSchedule where you can enter an address and see the year an appraiser will physically inspect it, and state law calls for a visit at least once every five years.

Mistakes found later go through an abatement, a written request to the Assessor. The county lists a homestead abatement (you must prove occupancy), a valuation and classification abatement, and a local option for disaster damage worth at least half of the structure. Keep paying while any of these is pending, since approval can take months.

sections.h2: What happens to my Sherburne County tax bill when I sell?
sections.html:
The bill does not disappear at the sale. Unpaid tax is settled at closing, usually from the seller's proceeds, so ask the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4350 for current amounts on the parcel before you set a closing date. If your lender escrows tax, ask for the escrow balance too.

One step belongs to you after a sale of a homesteaded house. The county's property tax page points to Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e), which requires you to tell the Assessor within 30 days when the house you homestead is sold or transferred, or when you change your primary residence. A change-of-address form is available on the county website.

The county's Print Tax Statement page lets you pull current statements by parcel, which gives you the figures a title company will ask for.

faqs.q: What are the Sherburne County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second half of real estate tax. Agricultural parcels owe the second half by November 15. Tax of $50 or less is due in full on May 15, and the postmark must show the due date or earlier.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Sherburne County property value?
faqs.a: Call the Assessor at 763-765-4900. The office is at 13880 Business Center Drive NW, Suite 100, in Elk River, and it handles valuation, classification, abatements and the first stage of an appeal.

faqs.q: Can I pay Sherburne County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, through Forte online or at 877-690-3729 with jurisdiction code 3307. Credit cards carry a 2.40% fee with a $2.00 minimum, eChecks cost $1.55, and debit cards cost $4.00. You will see the amount before you confirm.

faqs.q: Does Sherburne County have a county board of appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. After the local board, you may appear before the County Board of Appeal and Equalization at the Government Center, by appointment through the Auditor/Treasurer at 763-765-4351. The 2026 session was held on June 16, and the Tax Court route stays open until April 30 of the tax year.

faqs.q: What do I do about homestead status after selling a Sherburne County house?
faqs.a: Notify the county Assessor within 30 days of the sale or transfer. Minnesota Statute 273.124, subdivision 13 (e), sets that duty, and the county provides an online change-of-address form. Questions can go to the Assessor at 763-765-4900.
